newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai maize eases, soymeal firms this week.
newsitem.headline: Thai maize eases, soymeal firms this week.

text.p: Thai domestic maize prices paid by feed producers extended a steady decline to an average 4.20 baht/kg this week from 4.28 a week ago on increased supply from fresh domestic harvest, traders said on Tuesday.
A major feed producer said new Thai harvest, mostly from eastern Prachinburi and Chantaburi provinces and some from northeast and north central Thailand, was a major factor depressing prices.
The Thai Maize Association said a field survey early this month put the Thai 1996/97 (July/June) maize crop at a projected 4.20 million tonnes, against 4.06 million a year ago.
Bangkok soymeal prices firmed further to 9.90 baht/kg from 9.70 a week ago as the Thai market waits for Brazilian imports next month, traders said.
Traders said they expect about 10,000 tonnes of imported soymeal in September but its price is not immediately available.
A trader at Bangkok Produce said a small Thai rainy season soybean crop being harvest from late August to early October, and earlier limited soybean imports, had reduced local soymeal material.
He said due to red tape in cutting Thai import tariffs, soybean importers had failed to fill about 20,000 tonnes of an import quota by a July 31 deadline set by the commerce ministry.
The Thai Soymeal Traders and Importers Association said Thailand imported 23,441 tonnes of soymeal in June against 74,911 tonnes in May and 101,041 tonnes in April.
